TitanForge Inc. - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the TitanForge Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss TitanForge's results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; John Ramirez, Chief Financial Officer; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Operating Officer; and Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking in nature and subject to certain risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on TitanForge's performance for Q3 2024. We've made significant progress on several fronts, and I'd like to highlight a few key achievements. Our backlog has reached a record level, providing exceptional revenue visibility with strong conversion timelines across diverse segments. Revenue performance has been robust across geographic regions, reflecting our balanced global footprint. We've outlined clear capital expenditure plans prioritizing capacity expansion, digital transformation, and sustainability. Our guidance is underpinned by solid assumptions on economic growth and end-market demand in automation and electrification. Total revenue delivered strong year-over-year growth, driven by both organic expansion and strategic acquisitions. Order intake trends remain healthy by end market, with book-to-bill ratios above target in construction, mining, and agriculture. Organic revenue growth outpaced expectations, complemented by inorganic contributions. And total order intake grew impressively year-over-year, bolstering our backlog.

We are confident that our strategic initiatives are positioning us for long-term sustainable growth.

Now, I'll turn the call over to John Ramirez to provide more detail on our financial results.

John Ramirez (CFO):
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. I'll dive right into our top-line results, which reflect strong execution across our core segments in the industrial equipment space amid a resilient macro environment.

For the quarter, total revenue reached $2.85 billion, representing an 11% year-over-year increase on a reported basis and 12% on a constant currency basis. This marks our third consecutive quarter of double-digit growth and outperforms the broader industrial equipment market. On an organic basis—excluding the impact of our recent M&A activity and FX—growth was a robust 9.2%, accelerating from Q2 and ahead of our full-year midpoint guidance. Q3 organic expansion was broad-based across automation and robotics at 14.5%, heavy machinery at 6.8%, and precision components at 7.1%. Pricing discipline contributed about 4 points, with volumes up 7%, and aftermarket parts and services surging 15% due to our expanding telematics platform.

Regionally, this performance highlights our diversification: North America grew 19% to $5.98 billion year-to-date equivalent pace, fueled by reshoring and CHIPS Act tailwinds; EMEA up 13%; Asia-Pacific up 5% despite China softness, offset by India and Southeast Asia; and Latin America up 11%. By segment, machinery led at 18.3% growth, components at 9.1%, and services at 12.7%, now 45% of recurring revenue thanks to digital services like our IndusCloud platform.

Turning to inorganic contributions, acquisitions added 13.8 points to total growth YTD, led by our $650 million purchase of RoboForge Technologies, contributing $185 million in Q3 with $22 million in realized synergies from supply chain consolidation and cross-selling into EV battery lines for clients like BMW and Rivian. Our earlier Precision Gearworks tuck-in added another $42 million in high-margin wind and off-highway components. These bolt-ons have boosted EBITDA margins by 110 basis points and expanded our addressable market in electrification by 15%.

Now, let's discuss revenue performance by geographic region, which underscores our balanced footprint—Americas at 48%, EMEA 26%, Asia-Pacific 20%, Rest of World 6%. Americas delivered $1.37 billion, up 15% YoY, with North America at 17% on data center capex, electric wheel loaders, and IIJA-funded infrastructure where our autonomous dozers with Trimble integration saw 25% shipment growth. Mexico's nearshoring for Ford and GM drove CNC demand, mitigated by dual-sourcing and a new $250 million Monterrey facility for EV handlers.

EMEA posted $741 million, up 8%, with Europe at 9% on EU Green Deal hydrogen turbines and biomass systems up 22%, plus UK aftermarket surge via IndusConnect on 450,000 connected assets. Middle East mining equipment grew 15% on Vision 2030.

Asia-Pacific hit $570 million, up 10%, with China down 2% on real estate but India/Southeast up 25% on PLI robotics for Reliance/Tata and Indonesia nickel HPGR presses. Rest of World added $171 million, up 5%, led by Brazil agribusiness.

This diversification, with emerging markets now 28% of revenues, shields us amid headwinds, supported by $1.2 billion global capex and 85% backlog visibility for 2024.

Next, our backlog dynamics continue to provide exceptional revenue visibility in the industrial equipment sector. As of Q3 end, backlog stands at a record $2.85 billion, up 25% YoY from $2.28 billion and 8% sequentially from Q2's $2.64 billion. This reflects a 1.32x book-to-bill, above our 1.1x-1.2x target, equating to 2.1x trailing 12-month revenue run-rate and supporting FY24 guidance of $5.2-$5.4 billion with mid-teens organic growth in FY25.

By segment: Automation and Robotics 42% or $1.20 billion, up 35% YoY on Fanuc-integrated welding cells for Tesla/Foxconn EV lines; Machining and Forming 28% or $800 million, up 18% on five-axis CNC for Stellantis/PACCAR reshoring; Material Handling 20% or $570 million, up 22% mirroring Caterpillar's upcycle; Aerospace/Energy 10% or $280 million, up 45% on Boeing composites and IRA wind tooling.

Regionally: North America 52% or $1.48 billion, up 30% on CHIPS/Intel; EMEA 24% or $685 million, flat but improving; APAC 20% or $570 million, up 15% on TSMC/India PLI; Latin America 4% or $115 million on Mexico nearshoring.

Conversion timeline, refined via digital twin ERP dashboards from our $150 million Industry 4.0 spend: 38% or $1.08 billion short-term (Q4 FY24/Q1 FY25, $850-900 million revenue at 95%+ on-time, lead times down to 12-16 weeks); 32% medium-term cumulative 70% or $2.0 billion in FY25 via Rockford/Monterrey expansions; 30% long-tail or $855 million beyond FY25 on custom projects with <5% cancellation risk.

Accelerators include supply chain resilience (98% OTP, 70% North America/Mexico sourcing), EquipOS IoT on 60% of units cutting downtime 25%, and 11% higher ASPs at 55% margins. This positions $500 million+ upside from EV/semis/automation, with DSOs at 62 days and $400 million FY24 cash conversion.

Shifting to order intake, Q3 totaled $2.8 billion, up 18% YoY and 12% sequentially, driving 1.25x book-to-bill and $12.4 billion backlog for 14-month visibility. By end market: Construction 42% or $1.18 billion, up 22% at 1.32x on TE-500 excavators, NA leading on IIJA; Mining 28% or $780 million, up 25% at 1.40x on copper/lithium with BHP-like haul trucks and electric prototypes; Agriculture 18% or $500 million, up 8% at 1.10x on PrecisionAg tractors despite volatility; Others 12% including oil/gas up 15%.

Regionally balanced, with 22% electrified/autonomous orders from our Titan Forward initiative supporting 16% FY24 intake growth to $11.0-11.5 billion.

Total order intake specifically was $1.28 billion, up 18% YoY organically despite 2% FX headwind, ninth straight double-digit quarter at 1.25x book-to-bill, backlog $4.7 billion up 22% with 60% converting in 12 months. Automation/robotics up 32% to $520 million on semis/EV; Heavy Machinery 12% to $450 million on IIJA; Aerospace/Defense 9% to $310 million.

Before Q&A, a few words on capital expenditure plans, guiding FY24 CapEx at $650 million or 7.2% of revenue, up 22% YoY in line with peers like Caterpillar/Deere. Priorities: 45% or $292 million capacity expansion (e.g., $150 million Greenville SC for semi/EV via CHIPS/IRA, payback <3 years); 30% or $195 million automation/digital ($120 million cobots/AI via TIMConnect, OEE to 92%); 15% or $98 million sustainability (electrified presses, 20% energy cut); 10% maintenance/IT.

This multi-year $2.5-3 billion commitment targets 8-10% organic growth in semis/EVs/renewables, ROIC >15%, strong FCF at 90% conversion funding dividends/buybacks.

Finally, key assumptions for FY24 guidance of $4.85-5.05 billion revenue (7-11% organic), 18.5-19.5% EBITDA margins, $650-750 million FCF: Soft landing with US GDP 2.3%/2.0%, PMI mid-50s, PCE 2.5%, Fed peak 4.75%. End-markets: Factory automation 9%, semis 15%, aerospace flat-2%, energy 12%. Regions: NA 12%, APAC 8%, Europe 3%. Levers: MachineryOS digital thread (35% recurring by 2026), ESG compliance, supply resilience. Upside from Fed cuts/AI, buffered by 1.2x debt/EBITDA.

Gross margin was 55%, driven by pricing, mix, and cost normalization. Operating expenses $450 million, operating income $650 million, net income $420 million or $1.85 EPS.

We remain committed to disciplined capital allocation and maximizing shareholder value.

Now, I will hand over to Maria Gonzalez, COO, for an operational update.

Maria Gonzalez (COO):
Thank you, John. Operationally, we've optimized manufacturing processes with 92% asset utilization across Ohio, Mexico, and Europe plants, improving supply chain efficiency via dual-sourcing and vendor scorecards targeting 98% on-time performance. We've enhanced customer service with 20% faster commissioning through IoT pilots and focused on employee safety, achieving zero lost-time incidents. We're leveraging data analytics for OEE gains and upskilling via Rockwell partnerships. Supply chain headwinds like Red Sea are contained to 2% cost impact.

And I will turn the call over to our CTO, Dr. Elena Vasquez, for an update on our technology roadmap.

Dr. Elena Vasquez (CTO):
Thank you, Maria. We are committed to driving innovation with R&D investments up 12% to $650 million annually in AI, ML, robotics, and IoT. Our EquipOS platform on 60% of backlog enables predictive maintenance, reducing downtime 25% and ROI 15% faster for adopters like John Deere. New products like e-drive milling centers with 40% lower energy use and IntelliArm cobots are significantly impacting the market, with 22% of Q3 orders electrified/autonomous and design-wins at premium pricing. We're advancing additive manufacturing and hydrogen-ready systems to optimize customer operations and enhance performance.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from David Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Lee (Morgan Stanley):
Good morning. Can you discuss the long-term impact of the new EquipOS platform on your revenue and profitability?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thanks, David. The EquipOS IoT platform is transformative, embedded in 65% of new bookings and driving recurring revenue to 35% of total by 2026 via digital twins and edge AI, similar to Siemens MindSphere. Long-term, it lifts aftermarket attachment to 28%, with 20% customer retention uplift and margins expanding 240 basis points as seen YTD. Pilots show 25% downtime cuts, accelerating ROI and supporting 10%+ organic growth in automation/semis, de-risking FY25 visibility.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen (Goldman Sachs):
What are your expectations for revenue growth in the coming year?

John Ramirez:
Good question, Emily. For FY25, we see 10-13% total growth, with 8-10% organic from backlog conversion, semis/EV tailwinds, and pricing intact. Q4 FY24 accelerates mid-teens in Americas, 12-15% APAC rebound, EMEA low-single. Assumptions hold on soft landing, PMI expansion, no black swans—upside from AI capex/Fed cuts adds 2-3 points, buffered by $2.85 billion backlog covering 85% of FY25.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Patel with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Patel (JPMorgan):
Can you discuss your plans for expanding your global footprint?

Alex Rivera:
Absolutely, Mike. Our $1.2 billion capex emphasizes U.S. Southeast/Mexico for nearshoring (60% expansion spend), Europe Dortmund for REPowerEU, and Asia Singapore hub for 20% service attachment. Emerging markets now 28% revenues, up from 22%, via Monterrey EV plant, India PLI robotics, and USMCA localization at 70% for Tier 1s. This captures 20% CAGR EV/semicon growth, with Mexico adding 500k jobs and IRA/CHIPS fueling NA.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Lisa Wong (Barclays):
How are you managing rising energy costs?

Maria Gonzalez:
Thanks, Lisa. We've allocated $98 million CapEx to sustainability, retrofitting presses with Siemens drives for 20% energy intensity reduction and solar microgrids cutting grid reliance 15% in Europe. Heat recovery and low-emission fluids align with Scope 1/2 targets, securing $25 million DOE grants/IRA credits. Digital twins optimize via regenerative braking, containing costs at 2% impact vs. peers' 5%, with 98% uptime on connected assets.

Operator:
Thank you. [Operator Instructions for next, but as time concludes...]

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your interest in TitanForge. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Jenkins (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
